lessons.title: The Multiply Trick
lessons.summary: Learn the one idea behind most counting problems. When you make choices one after another, multiply.

lessons.title: When Order Matters
lessons.summary: Count lineups and arrangements, where each choice uses up an option, and learn why n factorial works.

lessons.title: Overcount, Then Divide
lessons.summary: When order doesn't matter, count as if it did, then divide out the repeats. This is where the "choose" formula comes from.

lessons.title: Count the Opposite
lessons.summary: When what you want is messy but what you don't want is tidy, count everything and subtract.

lessons.title: Split Into Cases
lessons.summary: When one rule makes a problem awkward, break it into separate cases, count each one, and add.

lessons.title: Place Value: What Digits Really Mean
lessons.summary: See that a number is a sum of its place values. That one idea solves digit puzzles and explains why many shortcuts work.

lessons.title: Mental Math Shortcuts
lessons.summary: Calculators aren't allowed on these contests. Learn to rearrange problems so that the arithmetic gets easy and you make fewer mistakes.

lessons.title: Divisibility Rules and Why They Work
lessons.summary: Tell whether a big number divides evenly without doing long division, and use place value to see why the rules are true.

lessons.title: Factors, Primes and Leftovers
lessons.summary: Factors come in pairs, so you can find them all without missing any. Then see how primes and leftovers fit the same idea.

lessons.title: Fractions as Equal Groups
lessons.summary: See what a fraction really means. Then find a fraction of a number, compare fractions, and add them without the most common mistakes.

lessons.title: Ratios as Boxes
lessons.summary: A ratio tells you how to make equal groups. Draw boxes, find what goes in one box, and most ratio problems fall into place.

lessons.title: Rates and Scaling
lessons.summary: Find the cost or amount for one, and scale up or down. Learn why growing means multiplying, not adding.

lessons.title: Percents
lessons.summary: A percent is a fraction out of 100. Build percents from easy pieces, and watch out for percents of a number that has changed.

lessons.title: Perimeter and Area
lessons.summary: Understand the difference between the distance around a shape and the space inside it, and see why knowing one doesn't tell you the other.

lessons.title: Triangle Area and Helper Lines
lessons.summary: See why a triangle is half of a rectangle, what height really means, and how drawing one extra line can solve a problem.

lessons.title: Three Angle Facts
lessons.summary: Learn the three angle facts that solve most beginner problems, see why they're true, and fill in a diagram one step at a time.

lessons.title: Split It or Subtract It
lessons.summary: Find the area of an unusual shape in two ways. Split it into pieces you know, or subtract the part you don't want.

lessons.title: A First Look at Right Triangles
lessons.summary: Use the Pythagorean Theorem to find a missing side of a right triangle, and learn the whole-number triangles that contests love.

lessons.title: Repeating and Growing Patterns
lessons.summary: Use remainders to jump ahead in a repeating pattern, and learn how to reach the 100th term of a growing one without off-by-one mistakes.

lessons.title: Try Small, Then Ask Why
lessons.summary: When a problem looks huge, solve tiny versions of it and look for a pattern. Then find the reason, because patterns can fool you.

lessons.title: Working Backwards
lessons.summary: When a problem tells you how something ended, start at the end and undo each step in reverse order.

lessons.title: Logic Tables and Pigeonholes
lessons.summary: Organize clues in a table, test every case when someone may be lying, and use the pigeonhole principle to prove that something must happen.

lessons.title: Count What You Want
lessons.summary: Probability is counting twice. Count the outcomes you want, count all of the outcomes, and divide.

lessons.title: List the Real Outcomes
lessons.summary: Two coins can land three ways, so why isn't each way one third? Learn to list outcomes that really are equally likely, using the two-dice table.

lessons.title: Tree Diagrams and Multiplying
lessons.summary: Draw a tree for chance with several steps. Multiply along a path, add between paths, and account for what changes when a marble isn't put back.

lessons.title: One Minus the Chance It Doesn't Happen
lessons.summary: When you see "at least one," flip the question. Find the chance of "none," subtract from 1, and tie it back to counting the opposite.

lessons.title: Solving and Translating
lessons.summary: Use a letter for the number you don't know, solve equations by keeping them balanced, and turn English sentences into math.

lessons.title: Age and Number Stories
lessons.summary: Organize stories about ages and digits in a table, so that each sentence turns into one clean equation.

lessons.title: Distance, Speed and Time
lessons.summary: Use one formula for every motion problem, and avoid the most famous trap, which is averaging two speeds.

lessons.title: Two Unknowns at Once
lessons.summary: Solve problems with two unknown numbers, by rewriting one in terms of the other or by adding equations together.

lessons.title: Working Together
lessons.summary: Find how long a job takes when people work together by asking how much each one gets done in one hour.

lessons.title: Overlaps and Venn Diagrams
lessons.summary: Count groups that overlap without double counting, using Venn diagrams filled in from the middle out.

lessons.title: Counting With Rules
lessons.summary: Handle lineups with rules by gluing together people who must sit together, and by placing others into gaps to keep them apart.

lessons.title: Arrangements With Repeats
lessons.summary: Count arrangements of things that repeat by dividing out swaps, and see how this connects to choosing spots.

lessons.title: Grid Paths and Choosing With Conditions
lessons.summary: Count routes on a street grid, then combine several choices at once when groups must follow rules.

lessons.title: Prime Factorization
lessons.summary: Every whole number is built from primes in exactly one way. Learn to find a number's prime factors, and use them to answer questions quickly.

lessons.title: Counting Divisors and Factorial Zeros
lessons.summary: Count a number's factors in seconds, without listing them, and find how many zeros a huge factorial ends with.

lessons.title: GCF and LCM
lessons.summary: Find the greatest common factor and least common multiple using primes, and learn how to tell which one a word problem needs.

lessons.title: Units Digits and Remainder Arithmetic
lessons.summary: Find the last digit of enormous powers, and do arithmetic using only remainders.

lessons.title: Angle Chasing
lessons.summary: Find unknown angles one step at a time using outside angles, parallel lines, and the angle sum of any polygon.

lessons.title: Why Pythagoras Works
lessons.summary: See a picture that proves the Pythagorean Theorem, and learn the two special right triangles that contests use most.

lessons.title: Helper Lines and Area Two Ways
lessons.summary: Draw a height to create a right triangle, find a triangle's area two different ways, and use the triangle inequality.

lessons.title: Similar Triangles
lessons.summary: Spot triangles with the same shape, use scale factors to find lengths you can't measure, and see why area grows by the square of the scale factor.

lessons.title: Circle Formulas and Scaling
lessons.summary: Understand what pi really is, and why the circumference and area formulas work. Then see what happens when a circle grows.

lessons.title: Shaded Regions
lessons.summary: Find the area of strange-looking shaded shapes by subtracting, by moving pieces around, or by splitting them up.

lessons.title: Slices of Circles and Probability With Area
lessons.summary: Treat a slice of a circle as a fraction of the whole, and use area to find probabilities when there's nothing to count.

lessons.title: Boxes, Cylinders and Picturing 3D
lessons.summary: Find volume by stacking layers and surface area by unfolding. Then learn to reason about shapes you can't see all of.

lessons.title: The Total Trick
lessons.summary: An average hides a total. Multiply to find it, and most average problems become one or two lines.

lessons.title: Median, Mode, Tables and Graphs
lessons.summary: Find the middle and the most common values, and read tables and graphs carefully, because that's where many points get lost.

lessons.title: Chance With Several Steps
lessons.summary: Use bigger trees to handle choices that lead to different situations, and add up every path that gets you what you want.

lessons.title: Expected Value
lessons.summary: Find what happens on average in a game of chance, and use casework to count your way through harder probability.

lessons.title: Multiplying Out and Difference of Squares
lessons.summary: Learn how two sums multiply, and then use the most useful pattern in contest algebra to turn huge calculations into quick ones.

lessons.title: Perfect Squares and the Missing Piece
lessons.summary: Squaring a sum has a middle part that people forget. Use that middle part to find values without ever solving for x or y.

lessons.title: Quadratics and Vieta's Formulas
lessons.summary: Solve quadratic equations by factoring, and learn what a quadratic's solutions add up to and multiply to, without finding them.

lessons.title: Add-One Factoring and Telescoping
lessons.summary: Two clever tricks. Add a number to make an expression factor, and watch long products and sums collapse.

lessons.title: Mod Notation and the Rules
lessons.summary: Learn the language of remainders, and find out which operations you can do with remainders alone, and which one you can't.

lessons.title: Giant Powers
lessons.summary: Find the remainder of enormous powers using cycles, stepping stones, and the trick of replacing a base with negative 1.

lessons.title: Several Conditions at Once
lessons.summary: Find a number that satisfies several remainder conditions by sieving, and learn when a solution has to exist.

lessons.title: Numbers in Other Bases
lessons.summary: See how our number system works by trying a different one. Convert between bases, and use base 2 to count and solve problems.

lessons.title: Arithmetic Sequences
lessons.summary: Find any term of a list that grows by the same amount each time, and work out the pattern from only two of its terms.

lessons.title: Adding Long Lists Fast
lessons.summary: Add an arithmetic sequence in one step by pairing the outside terms, and see why the average of the list does all of the work.

lessons.title: Geometric Sequences
lessons.summary: Work with lists that multiply by the same number each time, add them up with a neat trick, and even add up lists that never end.

lessons.title: Lists Built From a Rule
lessons.summary: Follow rules that build each term from the ones before it, find hidden cycles, and watch sums collapse when terms cancel.

lessons.title: Pascal's Triangle and Binomials
lessons.summary: See how choosing groups builds a famous triangle of numbers, and use it to count subsets and multiply out powers without doing the algebra.

lessons.title: Stars and Bars
lessons.summary: Count the ways to share identical things among people, by turning the problem into choosing spots in a row.

lessons.title: Counting Step by Step
lessons.summary: Count huge numbers of possibilities by asking how the last step could have happened, and building up from small cases. This is called recursion.

lessons.title: Harder Probability With Counting
lessons.summary: Combine all of your counting tools with probability, so that hard-looking chance questions become two counts and a fraction.

lessons.title: Stronger Similarity Tools
lessons.summary: Go beyond shadows. Find hidden similar triangles in right triangles and crossing lines, and use them to get lengths you couldn't find any other way.

lessons.title: Angles Inside a Circle
lessons.summary: Learn why an angle at the edge of a circle is half of the angle at the center, and use it to find angles that seem to have no connection.

lessons.title: Chords and Tangents
lessons.summary: Find lengths in circles using right angles at tangent points, equal tangents, and the products of pieces of crossing chords.

lessons.title: Circles With Other Shapes
lessons.summary: Find the circle inside or around a triangle, work with circles that touch, and combine everything from this unit.

lessons.title: Lines and Slopes
lessons.summary: Describe any straight line with two numbers. Then find where lines meet, tell when they're parallel or perpendicular, and count grid points on a line.

lessons.title: Distance, Midpoints and Circles
lessons.summary: Find the distance between two points with the Pythagorean Theorem, find midpoints by averaging, and write a circle as an equation.

lessons.title: Areas on a Grid
lessons.summary: Find the area of a tilted shape by boxing it in, or by using a neat pattern called the shoelace method.

lessons.title: Solving Geometry With Coordinates
lessons.summary: When a geometry problem feels stuck, put it on a grid. Choose smart coordinates, then let algebra find the answer. Learn reflections and rotations too.
